_comment: Shared config: tool_preheat.json
Read by TWO processors -- insert_missing_tool_preheat.py and
disable_unused_tool_temps.py -- hence the name, rather than being
named after either script individually.
target_lead_seconds: how many seconds before a tool needs heat its
heater should start ramping.
insert_missing_tool_preheat.py: applies this to a tool's FIRST use
in the print. OrcaSlicer's own ooze-prevention preheat only gives it
a fixed lead time (whatever your Ooze prevention 'preheat time'
setting is, typically ~30-40s); this script pushes that earlier when
there's enough print time available before the tool is first
needed, and inserts one from scratch when OrcaSlicer skipped it
entirely (no lead time was available near the very start of the
print).
disable_unused_tool_temps.py: uses this as the lead time for the
reheat it schedules after cooling down a tool that's idle mid-print.
It also feeds into the default idle-gap threshold (how long a tool
must be unneeded before it's worth cooling at all) -- see
target_cooldown_seconds below -- unless disable_unused_tool_temps.json's
idle_shutoff_minutes is set, which overrides just that threshold
decision, not the reheat lead time.
This is optional -- if this file is missing or unreadable, both
scripts fall back to a default of 90 seconds.
target_cooldown_seconds: how many seconds it takes a tool's heater to
actually cool down once commanded off. Read ONLY by
disable_unused_tool_temps.py, and only for its AUTO idle-gap
threshold (default idle_shutoff_minutes is unset): the threshold
becomes target_lead_seconds + target_cooldown_seconds, so a tool
only gets cycled off if the idle gap is long enough to both finish
cooling down AND still regain a full reheat lead time before it's
needed again. insert_missing_tool_preheat.py never reads this --
it doesn't cool anything down.
This is optional -- if missing, defaults to 0 (matches this
script's older behavior, threshold == target_lead_seconds alone).
Estimate it the same ballpark way as target_lead_seconds: how long
your hottest tool realistically takes to drop from print temp to
somewhere near idle once M104 S0 is sent. Doesn't need to be exact.
The 'earlier'/'reheat' position is estimated, not exact -- there's
no way to know real firmware timing without simulating acceleration,
so this calibrates a simple distance/feedrate model against
OrcaSlicer's own stated preheat times found elsewhere in the same
file (per tool, since each tool tends to print similar-shaped
regions on every layer). Expect it to land in the right ballpark,
not to the second.
